claim: Seipin is a protein that spans the ER membrane twice.
source: Here, we focused on Seipinopathy, a dominant motor neuron disease, based on the finding that its causal gene product, Seipin, is a protein that spans the ER membrane twice.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract as a known finding that forms the basis of the study.

claim: Gain-of-function mutations of Seipin produce non-glycosylated Seipin (ngSeipin).
source: Gain-of-function mutations of Seipin produce non-glycosylated Seipin (ngSeipin), which was previously shown to induce ER stress and apoptosis at both cell and mouse levels albeit with no clarified mechanism.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by previous literature.

claim: Non-glycosylated Seipin was previously shown to induce ER stress and apoptosis at both cell and mouse levels.
source: Gain-of-function mutations of Seipin produce non-glycosylated Seipin (ngSeipin), which was previously shown to induce ER stress and apoptosis at both cell and mouse levels albeit with no clarified mechanism.

claim: Aggregation-prone ngSeipin dominantly inactivated SERCA2b.
source: We found that aggregation-prone ngSeipin dominantly inactivated SERCA2b, the major calcium pump in the ER, and decreased the calcium concentration in the ER, leading to ER stress and apoptosis in human colorectal carcinoma-derived cells (HCT116).
evidence: Main finding of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: SERCA2b is the major calcium pump in the ER.
source: We found that aggregation-prone ngSeipin dominantly inactivated SERCA2b, the major calcium pump in the ER, and decreased the calcium concentration in the ER, leading to ER stress and apoptosis in human colorectal carcinoma-derived cells (HCT116).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: ngSeipin decreased the calcium concentration in the ER.
source: We found that aggregation-prone ngSeipin dominantly inactivated SERCA2b, the major calcium pump in the ER, and decreased the calcium concentration in the ER, leading to ER stress and apoptosis in human colorectal carcinoma-derived cells (HCT116).
evidence: Main finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Decreased calcium concentration in the ER leads to ER stress and apoptosis in HCT116 cells.
source: We found that aggregation-prone ngSeipin dominantly inactivated SERCA2b, the major calcium pump in the ER, and decreased the calcium concentration in the ER, leading to ER stress and apoptosis in human colorectal carcinoma-derived cells (HCT116).
evidence: Causal relationship stated in the abstract based on experimental findings.

claim: Inactivation of SERCA2b by ngSeipin required oligomerization of ngSeipin.
source: This inactivation required oligomerization of ngSeipin and direct interaction of the C-terminus of ngSeipin with SERCA2b, and was observed in Seipin-deficient neuroblastoma (SH-SY5Y) cells expressing ngSeipin at an endogenous protein level.
evidence: Mechanistic finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Inactivation of SERCA2b by ngSeipin required direct interaction of the C-terminus of ngSeipin with SERCA2b.
source: This inactivation required oligomerization of ngSeipin and direct interaction of the C-terminus of ngSeipin with SERCA2b, and was observed in Seipin-deficient neuroblastoma (SH-SY5Y) cells expressing ngSeipin at an endogenous protein level.
evidence: Mechanistic finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The inactivation of SERCA2b by ngSeipin was observed in Seipin-deficient neuroblastoma (SH-SY5Y) cells expressing ngSeipin at an endogenous protein level.
source: This inactivation required oligomerization of ngSeipin and direct interaction of the C-terminus of ngSeipin with SERCA2b, and was observed in Seipin-deficient neuroblastoma (SH-SY5Y) cells expressing ngSeipin at an endogenous protein level.
evidence: Experimental observation stated in the abstract.

claim: The BSCL1 gene encodes 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferase 2 (AGPAT2).
source: The BSCL1 gene encodes 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferase 2 (AGPAT2), which is present in the membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and involved in phospholipid biosynthesis (Agarwal et al., 2002; Garg et al., 1999), whereas the BSCL2 gene encodes Seipin, a protein which spans the ER membrane twice and whose function was unknown at that time (Magré et al., 2001).

claim: AGPAT2 is present in the membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and involved in phospholipid biosynthesis.
source: The BSCL1 gene encodes 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferase 2 (AGPAT2), which is present in the membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and involved in phospholipid biosynthesis (Agarwal et al., 2002; Garg et al., 1999), whereas the BSCL2 gene encodes Seipin, a protein which spans the ER membrane twice and whose function was unknown at that time (Magré et al., 2001).

claim: The BSCL2 gene encodes Seipin.
source: The BSCL1 gene encodes 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferase 2 (AGPAT2), which is present in the membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and involved in phospholipid biosynthesis (Agarwal et al., 2002; Garg et al., 1999), whereas the BSCL2 gene encodes Seipin, a protein which spans the ER membrane twice and whose function was unknown at that time (Magré et al., 2001).

claim: Loss-of-function mutations of the BSCL2 gene produce more severe symptoms than those of the BSCL1 gene.
source: Loss-of-function mutations of the BSCL2 gene appear to produce more severe symptoms than those of the BSCL1 gene (Van Maldergem et al., 2002).

claim: Seipin is involved in lipid droplet morphology in yeast.
source: Since the discovery that Seipin is involved in lipid droplet morphology in yeast (Szymanski et al., 2007), the role of Seipin in the biogenesis of lipid droplets has gained extensive attention (Bi et al., 2014; Cui et al., 2011; Sim et al., 2013; Sui et al., 2018; Tian et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2016; Yan et al., 2018).

claim: Two missense mutations of the BSCL2 gene, N152S and S154L of Seipin, dominantly cause distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) or distal muscular atrophy.
source: To our interest, two missense mutations of the BSCL2 gene, namely, N152S and S154L of Seipin, were found to dominantly cause distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) or distal muscular atrophy, which is characterized almost exclusively by the degeneration of motor nerve fibers, predominantly in the distal part of limbs (Windpassinger et al., 2004).

claim: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) is characterized almost exclusively by the degeneration of motor nerve fibers, predominantly in the distal part of limbs.
source: To our interest, two missense mutations of the BSCL2 gene, namely, N152S and S154L of Seipin, were found to dominantly cause distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) or distal muscular atrophy, which is characterized almost exclusively by the degeneration of motor nerve fibers, predominantly in the distal part of limbs (Windpassinger et al., 2004).

claim: N152, V153, and S154 of Seipin match the triplet code (Asn-X-Ser/Thr; X: any amino acid except Pro) for N-glycosylation.
source: Because N152, V153, and S154 of Seipin match the triplet code (Asn-X-Ser/Thr; X: any amino acid except Pro) for N-glycosylation, neither N152S nor S154L Seipin are glycosylated, leading to the proposal that the production of these aggregation-prone mutants results in neurodegeneration (Windpassinger et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about N-glycosylation consensus sequence.

claim: Neither N152S nor S154L Seipin are glycosylated.
source: Because N152, V153, and S154 of Seipin match the triplet code (Asn-X-Ser/Thr; X: any amino acid except Pro) for N-glycosylation, neither N152S nor S154L Seipin are glycosylated, leading to the proposal that the production of these aggregation-prone mutants results in neurodegeneration (Windpassinger et al., 2004).
evidence: Logical inference from the disruption of the N-glycosylation consensus sequence.

claim: The production of aggregation-prone N152S and S154L Seipin mutants results in neurodegeneration.
source: Because N152, V153, and S154 of Seipin match the triplet code (Asn-X-Ser/Thr; X: any amino acid except Pro) for N-glycosylation, neither N152S nor S154L Seipin are glycosylated, leading to the proposal that the production of these aggregation-prone mutants results in neurodegeneration (Windpassinger et al., 2004).

claim: Seipin has two splice variants, a short form of 398 aa and long form of 462 aa.
source: Seipin was first identified as a protein of 398 aa (Magré et al., 2001), and later found (Lundin et al., 2006) to have two splice variants, a short form of 398 aa and long form of 462 aa (see Figure 1A), which are translated from three Seipin mRNA isoforms of 1.6 kb, 1.8 kb, and 2.2 kb.
evidence: Cited from previous literature and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Both short and long forms of Seipin are translatable from 1.8 kb and 2.2 kb mRNA, but the long form is more abundantly produced than the short form.
source: Both forms are translatable from 1.8 kb and 2.2 kb mRNA, but the long form is more abundantly produced than the short form.

claim: Only the short form of Seipin is translated from 1.6 kb mRNA.
source: In contrast, only the short form is translated from 1.6 kb mRNA (Lundin et al., 2006).

claim: 1.8 kb mRNA is predominantly expressed in human brain.
source: Because 1.8 kb mRNA is predominantly expressed in human brain (Magré et al., 2001), it is considered that human brain expresses mainly the long form (Cartwright and Goodman, 2012).

claim: Human brain expresses mainly the long form of Seipin.
source: Because 1.8 kb mRNA is predominantly expressed in human brain (Magré et al., 2001), it is considered that human brain expresses mainly the long form (Cartwright and Goodman, 2012).
evidence: Inference from mRNA expression data, cited from previous literature.

claim: HCT116 cells expressed only the short form of Seipin (SeipinS).
source: We found that human HCT116 diploid cells derived from colorectal carcinoma (Roschke et al., 2002), which we use exclusively for gene knockout analysis, expressed only the short form of Seipin, designated SeipinS, whereas human neuroblastoma-derived SH-SY5Y cells with trisomy 7 (Yusuf et al., 2013) expressed both SeipinS and the long form of Seipin, designated SeipinL, and further showed that SeipinS and SeipinL were both sensitive to digestion with endoglycosidase H (Endo H) (Figure 1B(a); note that the same amounts of total proteins [10 μg] in cell lysates were analyzed).

claim: SH-SY5Y cells expressed both SeipinS and the long form of Seipin (SeipinL).
source: We found that human HCT116 diploid cells derived from colorectal carcinoma (Roschke et al., 2002), which we use exclusively for gene knockout analysis, expressed only the short form of Seipin, designated SeipinS, whereas human neuroblastoma-derived SH-SY5Y cells with trisomy 7 (Yusuf et al., 2013) expressed both SeipinS and the long form of Seipin, designated SeipinL, and further showed that SeipinS and SeipinL were both sensitive to digestion with endoglycosidase H (Endo H) (Figure 1B(a); note that the same amounts of total proteins [10 μg] in cell lysates were analyzed).

claim: SeipinS and SeipinL were both sensitive to digestion with endoglycosidase H (Endo H).
source: We found that human HCT116 diploid cells derived from colorectal carcinoma (Roschke et al., 2002), which we use exclusively for gene knockout analysis, expressed only the short form of Seipin, designated SeipinS, whereas human neuroblastoma-derived SH-SY5Y cells with trisomy 7 (Yusuf et al., 2013) expressed both SeipinS and the long form of Seipin, designated SeipinL, and further showed that SeipinS and SeipinL were both sensitive to digestion with endoglycosidase H (Endo H) (Figure 1B(a); note that the same amounts of total proteins [10 μg] in cell lysates were analyzed).

claim: SH-SY5Y cells expressed Seipin mRNA five times more abundantly than HCT116 cells.
source: When normalized by the level of GAPDH, which was quite similarly detected by immunoblotting in cell lysates prepared from the same number (1.2 × 104 cells) of HCT116 and SH-SY5Y cells (data not shown), quantitative RT-PCR showed that SH-SY5Y cells expressed Seipin mRNA five times more abundantly than HCT116 cells (Figure 1B(b)).
evidence: Quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B(b).

claim: In humans, Seipin mRNA is highly expressed in the nervous system compared with other tissues except for testis.
source: Of note, searching the RNA sequencing database 'Expression Atlas: Gene expression across species and biological conditions' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gxa/home) showed that, in humans, Seipin mRNA is highly expressed in the nervous system compared with other tissues except for testis, whereas SERCA2 mRNA is relatively ubiquitously expressed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; GTEx Consortium, 2015; Papatheodorou et al., 2020).
evidence: Data from RNA sequencing database shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: SERCA2 mRNA is relatively ubiquitously expressed in humans.
source: Of note, searching the RNA sequencing database 'Expression Atlas: Gene expression across species and biological conditions' (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gxa/home) showed that, in humans, Seipin mRNA is highly expressed in the nervous system compared with other tissues except for testis, whereas SERCA2 mRNA is relatively ubiquitously expressed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; GTEx Consortium, 2015; Papatheodorou et al., 2020).
evidence: Data from RNA sequencing database shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: N-terminally Myc-tagged WT SeipinL was sensitive to digestion with Endo H.
source: When expressed in HCT116 cells by transfection, N-terminally Myc-tagged WT SeipinL was sensitive to digestion with Endo H but N-terminally Myc-tagged mutant (N152S/S154L) SeipinL was not, as expected (Figure 1A, bottom); WT SeipinL and the non-glycosylated mutant SeipinL are hereafter designated wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL, respectively.

claim: N-terminally Myc-tagged mutant (N152S/S154L) SeipinL was not sensitive to digestion with Endo H.
source: When expressed in HCT116 cells by transfection, N-terminally Myc-tagged WT SeipinL was sensitive to digestion with Endo H but N-terminally Myc-tagged mutant (N152S/S154L) SeipinL was not, as expected (Figure 1A, bottom); WT SeipinL and the non-glycosylated mutant SeipinL are hereafter designated wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL, respectively.

claim: Seipin physically associates with SERCA in fly.
source: We focused on SERCA2, the major calcium pump in the ER incorporating cytosolic calcium ion into the ER, based on the previous observation that Seipin physically associates with SERCA in fly as well as with SERCA2 in HEK293 cells (Bi et al., 2014).

claim: Seipin physically associates with SERCA2 in HEK293 cells.
source: We focused on SERCA2, the major calcium pump in the ER incorporating cytosolic calcium ion into the ER, based on the previous observation that Seipin physically associates with SERCA in fly as well as with SERCA2 in HEK293 cells (Bi et al., 2014).

claim: The expression level of SERCA2 dominated that of SERCA1 and SERCA3 in both HCT116 and SH-SY5Y cells.
source: It should be noted that the expression level of SERCA2 dominated that of SERCA1 and SERCA3 in both HCT116 and SH-SY5Y cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A(a, b)).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: SERCA2b is ubiquitously expressed.
source: It is also known that three splice variants exist for SERCA2 (Gélébart et al., 2003) and that SERCA2b is ubiquitously expressed, whereas SERCA2a and SERCA2c are expressed mainly in myocardium and skeletal muscle, in which the expression level of SERCA2b is low (Dally et al., 2006).

claim: SERCA2a and SERCA2c are expressed mainly in myocardium and skeletal muscle.
source: It is also known that three splice variants exist for SERCA2 (Gélébart et al., 2003) and that SERCA2b is ubiquitously expressed, whereas SERCA2a and SERCA2c are expressed mainly in myocardium and skeletal muscle, in which the expression level of SERCA2b is low (Dally et al., 2006).

claim: The expression level of SERCA2b dominated that of SERCA2a and SERCA2c in both HCT116 and SH-SY5Y cells.
source: Indeed, the expression level of SERCA2b dominated that of SERCA2a and SERCA2c in both HCT116 and SH-SY5Y cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B(a, b)).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The level of SERCA2b mRNA in SH-SY5Y cells was comparable with that in HCT116 cells.
source: Of note, quantitative RT-PCR showed that the level of SERCA2b mRNA in SH-SY5Y cells was comparable with that in HCT116 cells (Figure 1B(c)) and immunoblotting showed that the level of SERCA2b protein in SH-SY5Y cells was also comparable with that in HCT116 cells (Figure 1B(d)).
evidence: Quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B(c).

claim: The level of SERCA2b protein in SH-SY5Y cells was comparable with that in HCT116 cells.
source: Of note, quantitative RT-PCR showed that the level of SERCA2b mRNA in SH-SY5Y cells was comparable with that in HCT116 cells (Figure 1B(c)) and immunoblotting showed that the level of SERCA2b protein in SH-SY5Y cells was also comparable with that in HCT116 cells (Figure 1B(d)).

claim: ngSeipinL bound to SERCA2b more extensively than wtSeipinL.
source: Interestingly, immunoprecipitation from HCT116 cells expressing wtSeipinL or ngSeipinL by transfection showed that ngSeipinL bound to SERCA2b more extensively than wtSeipinL (Figure 1C).

claim: Expression of ngSeipinL in HCT116 cells markedly decreased [Ca2+] in the ER compared with that of wtSeipinL.
source: Expression of ngSeipinL in HCT116 cells by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) markedly decreased [Ca2+] in the ER compared with that of wtSeipinL (Figure 1E(a, b)).

claim: The effect of ngSeipinL on [Ca2+] in the ER was also observed in SH-SY5Y cells.
source: This effect of ngSeipinL on [Ca2+] in the ER was also observed in SH-SY5Y cells (Figure 1F(a, b)).

claim: Small amounts (~20%) of wtSeipinS and ngSeipinS were produced from transfected plasmid.
source: We noted that small amounts (~20%) of wtSeipinS and ngSeipinS were produced from transfected plasmid (Figure 1E(c)).

claim: wtSeipinS and ngSeipinS were likely translated from the second methionine M65.
source: Because they were not detected with anti-Myc antibody (data not shown), it is likely that they were translated from the second methionine M65 (see Figure 1A), given that the nucleotide sequences around M65 (ccgGccATGG) are more similar to the Kozak consensus sequence for translational initiation (gccRccATGG) than those around M1 (aggAagATGt).
evidence: Inference based on Kozak consensus sequence and experimental observation.

claim: The ER contains two types of calcium channel, namely, ryanodine receptor (RyR) and IP3 receptor (IP3R).
source: The ER contains two types of calcium channel, namely, ryanodine receptor (RyR) and IP3 receptor (IP3R), which release stored calcium to the cytosol upon various stimuli, for example, 4-chloro-m-cresol (4CmC) for RyR (Zorzato et al., 1993) and bradykinin for IP3R (Cruzblanca et al., 1998).
evidence: Established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: RyR and IP3R release stored calcium to the cytosol upon various stimuli.
source: The ER contains two types of calcium channel, namely, ryanodine receptor (RyR) and IP3 receptor (IP3R), which release stored calcium to the cytosol upon various stimuli, for example, 4-chloro-m-cresol (4CmC) for RyR (Zorzato et al., 1993) and bradykinin for IP3R (Cruzblanca et al., 1998).
evidence: Established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: 4-chloro-m-cresol (4CmC) stimulates RyR.
source: The ER contains two types of calcium channel, namely, ryanodine receptor (RyR) and IP3 receptor (IP3R), which release stored calcium to the cytosol upon various stimuli, for example, 4-chloro-m-cresol (4CmC) for RyR (Zorzato et al., 1993) and bradykinin for IP3R (Cruzblanca et al., 1998).

claim: Bradykinin stimulates IP3R.
source: The ER contains two types of calcium channel, namely, ryanodine receptor (RyR) and IP3 receptor (IP3R), which release stored calcium to the cytosol upon various stimuli, for example, 4-chloro-m-cresol (4CmC) for RyR (Zorzato et al., 1993) and bradykinin for IP3R (Cruzblanca et al., 1998).

claim: HCT116 cells express mRNA encoding RyR1, IP3R1, IP3R2, and IP3R3.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR detected expression of mRNA encoding RyR1, IP3R1, IP3R2, and IP3R3 in HCT116 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: RyR and IP3R are still active in HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL.
source: The lowered [Ca2+] in the ER of HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) compared with those expressing wtSeipinL (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D(d); compare bars 5, 11, and 17 with bars 3, 9, and 15) was further decreased upon treatment with 4CmC, bradykinin, or both (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D(d); compare bar 6 with bar 5, bar 12 with bar 11, bar 18 with bar 17), suggesting that RyR and IP3R are still active in HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL.
evidence: Inference from experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Thapsigargin treatment rapidly increases [Ca2+] in cytosol by inhibiting SERCA1/2/3 without affecting RyR or IP3R.
source: Thapsigargin treatment rapidly increases [Ca2+] in cytosol by inhibiting SERCA1/2/3 without affecting RyR or IP3R (Lytton et al., 1991).

claim: The total amount of calcium released from the ER to cytosol upon thapsigargin treatment was markedly decreased in HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL compared with those expressing wtSeipinL.
source: The total amount of calcium released from the ER to cytosol upon thapsigargin treatment, which was monitored using GCaMP6f, was markedly decreased in HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) compared with those expressing wtSeipinL (Figure 2A), reflecting lowered [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 1E), which was monitored using G-CEPIA1er.

claim: CDN1163 is a SERCA2 activator.
source: The treatment of HCT116 cells or HCT116 cells expressing wtSeipinL by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) with CDN1163, a SERCA2 activator (Cornea et al., 2013; Gruber et al., 2014), increased [Ca2+] in the ER, as expected, whereas the treatment of HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) with CDN1163 did not do (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).

claim: Treatment with CDN1163 increased [Ca2+] in the ER of HCT116 cells expressing wtSeipinL.
source: The treatment of HCT116 cells or HCT116 cells expressing wtSeipinL by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) with CDN1163, a SERCA2 activator (Cornea et al., 2013; Gruber et al., 2014), increased [Ca2+] in the ER, as expected, whereas the treatment of HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) with CDN1163 did not do (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treatment with CDN1163 did not increase [Ca2+] in the ER of HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL.
source: The treatment of HCT116 cells or HCT116 cells expressing wtSeipinL by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) with CDN1163, a SERCA2 activator (Cornea et al., 2013; Gruber et al., 2014), increased [Ca2+] in the ER, as expected, whereas the treatment of HCT116 cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection (10.4 ng/cm2) with CDN1163 did not do (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: ngSeipinL selectively inactivates SERCA2b.
source: These results suggest that ngSeipinL selectively inactivates SERCA2b.

claim: Expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at 5.20 and 10.4 ng/cm2 decreased [Ca2+] in the ER in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at 5.20 and 10.4 ng/cm2 decreased [Ca2+] in the ER in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B(a, b); compare bars 3 and 8 with bar 1), whereas expression of wtSeipinL by transfection at 5.20 and 10.4 ng/cm2 did not do (Figure 2B(a, b); compare bars 2 and 4 with bar 1).

claim: Expression of wtSeipinL by transfection at 5.20 and 10.4 ng/cm2 did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: Expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at 5.20 and 10.4 ng/cm2 decreased [Ca2+] in the ER in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B(a, b); compare bars 3 and 8 with bar 1), whereas expression of wtSeipinL by transfection at 5.20 and 10.4 ng/cm2 did not do (Figure 2B(a, b); compare bars 2 and 4 with bar 1).

claim: Co-expression of wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL decreased [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: Co-expression of wtSeipinL in a decreasing manner by transfection at 7.80, 5.20, and 2.60 ng/cm2 and of ngSeipinL in an increasing manner by transfection at 2.60, 5.20, and 7.80 ng/cm2 (transfection at a total of 10.4 ng/cm2) decreased [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 2B(a, b); compare bars 5, 6, and 7 with bar 1).

claim: CDN1163 treatment did not increase [Ca2+] in the ER significantly in HCT116 cells co-expressing wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL.
source: Furthermore, CDN1163 treatment did not increase [Ca2+] in the ER significantly in HCT116 cells co-expressing wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL by transfection (5.20 ng/cm2 each), in contrast to the case of untransfected HCT116 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: ngSeipinL dominantly inactivates SERCA2b and thereby dominantly decreases [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: Thus, ngSeipinL dominantly inactivates SERCA2b and thereby dominantly decreases [Ca2+] in the ER.

claim: [Ca2+] in the ER was decreased in Seipin-KO cells by 20–30% compared with WT cells.
source: [Ca2+] in the ER was decreased in Seipin-KO cells by 20–30% compared with WT cells (Figure 3A(a, b); compare bar 2 with bar 1), consistent with an ~30% decrease in SERCA activity in Seipin mutant fly compared with WT fly and with Bi et al.'s proposal that Seipin aids the maintenance of calcium homeostasis in the ER by binding to SERCA (Bi et al., 2014).

claim: There is an ~30% decrease in SERCA activity in Seipin mutant fly compared with WT fly.
source: [Ca2+] in the ER was decreased in Seipin-KO cells by 20–30% compared with WT cells (Figure 3A(a, b); compare bar 2 with bar 1), consistent with an ~30% decrease in SERCA activity in Seipin mutant fly compared with WT fly and with Bi et al.'s proposal that Seipin aids the maintenance of calcium homeostasis in the ER by binding to SERCA (Bi et al., 2014).

claim: Seipin aids the maintenance of calcium homeostasis in the ER by binding to SERCA.
source: [Ca2+] in the ER was decreased in Seipin-KO cells by 20–30% compared with WT cells (Figure 3A(a, b); compare bar 2 with bar 1), consistent with an ~30% decrease in SERCA activity in Seipin mutant fly compared with WT fly and with Bi et al.'s proposal that Seipin aids the maintenance of calcium homeostasis in the ER by binding to SERCA (Bi et al., 2014).

claim: Expression of both wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells at a low level restored [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: Expression of both wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells at a low level by transfection at 0.52 ng/cm2, which was comparable with the level of endogenous SeipinS (Figure 3A(c); compare lanes 3 and 4 with lane 1), restored [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 3A(a, b); compare bars 3 and 4 with bars 1 and 2).

claim: Higher expression of ngSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells decreased [Ca2+] in the ER in dose-dependent manner more robustly than that of wtSeipinL.
source: In contrast, a higher expression of ngSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells by transfection at >2.60 ng/cm2 decreased [Ca2+] in the ER in dose-dependent manner more robustly than that of wtSeipinL (Figure 3A(a, b); compare bars 6, 8, and 10 with bars 5, 7, and 9).

claim: Higher expression of ngSeipinL induced ER stress more extensively than that of wtSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells.
source: Higher expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at >2.60 ng/cm2 induced ER stress more extensively than that of wtSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells, as evidenced by increased levels of BiP mRNA (a target of the ATF6 pathway), XBP1(S) mRNA (a target of the IRE1 pathway), and CHOP mRNA (a target of the PERK pathway) (Figure 3B; compare bars 6, 8, and 10 with bars 5, 7, and 9).

claim: BiP mRNA is a target of the ATF6 pathway.
source: Higher expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at >2.60 ng/cm2 induced ER stress more extensively than that of wtSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells, as evidenced by increased levels of BiP mRNA (a target of the ATF6 pathway), XBP1(S) mRNA (a target of the IRE1 pathway), and CHOP mRNA (a target of the PERK pathway) (Figure 3B; compare bars 6, 8, and 10 with bars 5, 7, and 9).

claim: XBP1(S) mRNA is a target of the IRE1 pathway.
source: Higher expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at >2.60 ng/cm2 induced ER stress more extensively than that of wtSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells, as evidenced by increased levels of BiP mRNA (a target of the ATF6 pathway), XBP1(S) mRNA (a target of the IRE1 pathway), and CHOP mRNA (a target of the PERK pathway) (Figure 3B; compare bars 6, 8, and 10 with bars 5, 7, and 9).

claim: CHOP mRNA is a target of the PERK pathway.
source: Higher expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at >2.60 ng/cm2 induced ER stress more extensively than that of wtSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells, as evidenced by increased levels of BiP mRNA (a target of the ATF6 pathway), XBP1(S) mRNA (a target of the IRE1 pathway), and CHOP mRNA (a target of the PERK pathway) (Figure 3B; compare bars 6, 8, and 10 with bars 5, 7, and 9).

claim: Higher expression of ngSeipinL induced apoptosis more extensively than that of wtSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells.
source: Higher expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at >2.60 ng/cm2 induced apoptosis more extensively than that of wtSeipinL in Seipin-KO cells, as shown by increased detection of cleaved Caspase-3 by immunofluorescence (Figure 3C(a, b); compare bars 6, 8, and 10 with bars 5, 7, and 9).

claim: The PERK pathway is important in ER stress-induced apoptosis caused by ngSeipin.
source: Of note, clear-cut difference in the effect on [Ca2+] in the ER and apoptosis between transfection of ngSeipin at 0.52 ng/cm2 (not significant) and >2.60 ng/cm2 (significant) (Figure 3A(a, b) and C(a, b)) is best reflected in the induction of CHOP (Figure 3B), suggesting the importance of the PERK pathway in this ER stress-induced apoptosis.
evidence: Inference from experimental data shown in Figures 3A, 3B, and 3C.

claim: ngSeipinL expression-mediated decrease in [Ca2+] in the ER is a key factor in the development of Seipinopathy.
source: These results suggest that ngSeipinL expression-mediated decrease in [Ca2+] in the ER is a key factor in the development of Seipinopathy.

claim: Human Seipin exists as a wheel-like undecamer.
source: To elucidate the mechanism by which ngSeipinL inactivates SERCA2b, we examined the effect of oligomerization of Seipin because human Seipin exists as a wheel-like undecamer (Figure 4A; Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from previous literature and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Fly Seipin consisting of 370 aa is not glycosylated and exists as a wheel-shaped dodecamer.
source: Interestingly, fly Seipin consisting of 370 aa is not glycosylated and exists as a wheel-shaped dodecamer (Sui et al., 2018).

claim: N-glycan wedges the interface of two protomers in human Seipin.
source: Because N-glycan wedges the interface of two protomers in the case of human Seipin (Figure 4A, right panel), we hypothesized that non-glycosylated human Seipin expressed at a higher level becomes unable to maintain the undecamer structure, leading to aggregation.
evidence: Observation from structural data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Non-glycosylated human Seipin expressed at a higher level becomes unable to maintain the undecamer structure, leading to aggregation.
source: Because N-glycan wedges the interface of two protomers in the case of human Seipin (Figure 4A, right panel), we hypothesized that non-glycosylated human Seipin expressed at a higher level becomes unable to maintain the undecamer structure, leading to aggregation.

claim: The luminal region of each Seipin monomer consists of 8 β-strands, termed the β-sandwich domain, and 3 α-helices.
source: Structural analysis revealed that the luminal region of each Seipin monomer consists of 8 β-strands, termed the β-sandwich domain, and 3 α-helices, and that an ER membrane-anchored core ring is formed when the 3 α-helices of each of 11 monomers are gathered via multiple hydrophobic interactions between one protomer and its neighboring protomer, including those between L226 and L220 and between L233 and V227.

claim: An ER membrane-anchored core ring is formed when the 3 α-helices of each of 11 monomers are gathered via multiple hydrophobic interactions.
source: Structural analysis revealed that the luminal region of each Seipin monomer consists of 8 β-strands, termed the β-sandwich domain, and 3 α-helices, and that an ER membrane-anchored core ring is formed when the 3 α-helices of each of 11 monomers are gathered via multiple hydrophobic interactions between one protomer and its neighboring protomer, including those between L226 and L220 and between L233 and V227.

claim: The core ring is surrounded by 11 β-sandwich domains that are tightly associated via hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions.
source: The core ring is surrounded by 11 β-sandwich domains that are tightly associated via hydrogen bonds between one protomer and its neighboring protomer, including those between S181 and Y215, between Q239 and S217, and between H131 and R209; and via hydrophobic interactions between one protomer and its neighboring protomer, including those between Y134 and M189 (Figure 4A, right panel; Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from structural analysis and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Simultaneous mutation of six amino acids (H131R, Y134A, Y215A, L220D, L233D, and Q239A) prevents oligomerization of Seipin.
source: We therefore simultaneously mutated the six amino acids in wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL (H131R, Y134A, Y215A, L220D, L233D, and Q239A, Figure 4B), as previously reported to prevent oligomerization (Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from previous literature and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: SeipinL(M6) and ngSeipinL(M6) were still sensitive and insensitive, respectively, to digestion with EndoH.
source: Resulting SeipinL(M6) and ngSeipinL(M6) were still sensitive and insensitive, respectively, to digestion with EndoH, as expected (Figure 4C).

claim: Myc-tagged ngSeipinL and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL co-expressed at >1.30 ng/cm2 each produced a markedly strong PLA signal compared with co-expression of Myc-tagged wtSeipinL and Flag-tagged wtSeipinL.
source: Results showed the production of a markedly strong signal when Myc-tagged ngSeipinL and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL were co-expressed by transfection each at >1.30 ng/cm2 (total at >2.60 ng/cm2) compared with co-expression of Myc-tagged wtSeipinL and Flag-tagged wtSeipinL (Figure 4E(a, b); compare dot plot 4 with dot plot 3, dot plot 6 with dot plot 5, and dot plot 8 with dot plot 7), as we expected.

claim: The PLA signal was diminished when Myc-tagged ngSeipinL(M6) and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL(M6) were co-expressed.
source: Importantly, this signal was diminished when Myc-tagged ngSeipinL(M6) and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL(M6) were co-expressed by transfection each at 5.20 ng/cm2 (total at 10.4 ng/cm2) (Figure 4E(a, b); compare dot plot 10 with dot plot 8), supporting our hypothesis of non-glycosylated Seipin oligomer (undecamer)-dependent aggregation when expressed at a higher level.

claim: Non-glycosylated Seipin oligomer (undecamer)-dependent aggregation occurs when expressed at a higher level.
source: Importantly, this signal was diminished when Myc-tagged ngSeipinL(M6) and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL(M6) were co-expressed by transfection each at 5.20 ng/cm2 (total at 10.4 ng/cm2) (Figure 4E(a, b); compare dot plot 10 with dot plot 8), supporting our hypothesis of non-glycosylated Seipin oligomer (undecamer)-dependent aggregation when expressed at a higher level.

claim: ngSeipinL(M6) associates with SERCA2b.
source: Accordingly, although immunoprecipitation showed the association of ngSeipinL(M6) with SERCA2b (Figure 5A), ngSeipinL(M6) introduced into Seipin-KO cells by transfection even at 10.4 ng/cm2 (highest transfection level in this report) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 5B), did not induce ER stress (Figure 5C), and did not induce apoptosis (Figure 5D), in marked contrast to ngSeipinL.

claim: ngSeipinL(M6) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: Accordingly, although immunoprecipitation showed the association of ngSeipinL(M6) with SERCA2b (Figure 5A), ngSeipinL(M6) introduced into Seipin-KO cells by transfection even at 10.4 ng/cm2 (highest transfection level in this report) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 5B), did not induce ER stress (Figure 5C), and did not induce apoptosis (Figure 5D), in marked contrast to ngSeipinL.

claim: ngSeipinL(M6) did not induce ER stress.
source: Accordingly, although immunoprecipitation showed the association of ngSeipinL(M6) with SERCA2b (Figure 5A), ngSeipinL(M6) introduced into Seipin-KO cells by transfection even at 10.4 ng/cm2 (highest transfection level in this report) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 5B), did not induce ER stress (Figure 5C), and did not induce apoptosis (Figure 5D), in marked contrast to ngSeipinL.

claim: ngSeipinL(M6) did not induce apoptosis.
source: Accordingly, although immunoprecipitation showed the association of ngSeipinL(M6) with SERCA2b (Figure 5A), ngSeipinL(M6) introduced into Seipin-KO cells by transfection even at 10.4 ng/cm2 (highest transfection level in this report) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 5B), did not induce ER stress (Figure 5C), and did not induce apoptosis (Figure 5D), in marked contrast to ngSeipinL.

claim: SERCA2b is incorporated into aggregates of oligomerized ngSeipinL to be inactivated.
source: These results suggest that SERCA2b is incorporated into aggregates of oligomerized ngSeipinL to be inactivated.

claim: Flag-tagged ngSeipinL formed aggregates with Myc-tagged wtSeipin more extensively than Flag-tagged ngSeipinL(M6).
source: Of note, Flag-tagged ngSeipinL formed aggregates with Myc-tagged wtSeipin more extensively than Flag-tagged ngSeipinL(M6) when analyzed by PLA (Figure 4E(a, b); compare dot plot 11 with dot blot 13), indicative of its dominant nature.

claim: Only SeipinL(ΔC) and ngSeipinL(ΔC) were hardly co-immunoprecipitated with SERCA2b.
source: Immunoprecipitation using anti-SERCA2 antibody revealed that only SeipinL(ΔC) and ngSeipinL(ΔC) were hardly co-immunoprecipitated with SERCA2b (Figure 6C, lanes 10 and 11, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, lanes 23 and 24).
evidence: Immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Seipin(Cterm) was efficiently co-immunoprecipitated with SERCA2b.
source: We thus constructed a mutant that expresses only the C-terminal region of SeipinL and found that this Seipin(Cterm) was efficiently co-immunoprecipitated with SERCA2b (Figure 6C, lane 12).

claim: The cytosolic C-terminal region of SeipinL is necessary and sufficient for interaction with SERCA2b.
source: These findings indicate that the cytosolic C-terminal region of SeipinL is necessary and sufficient for interaction with SERCA2b.

claim: ngSeipinL(ΔC) lost the ability to decrease [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: In contrast, ngSeipinL(ΔC) lost the ability to decrease [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 6D; compare bar 13 with bar 12), indicating that direct interaction with SERCA2b is critical.

claim: Direct interaction with SERCA2b is critical for ngSeipinL to decrease [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: In contrast, ngSeipinL(ΔC) lost the ability to decrease [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 6D; compare bar 13 with bar 12), indicating that direct interaction with SERCA2b is critical.

claim: SeipinL(ΔLD) and Seipin(Cterm) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: Of note, SeipinL(ΔLD) and Seipin(Cterm) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 6D, yellow bars 9 and 14), although they were co-immunoprecipitated with SERCA2b (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, lane 20, and Figure 6C, lane 12).

claim: Both the luminal and C-terminal regions of ngSeipinL are required for inactivation of SERCA2b.
source: Given that the luminal region contains the six amino acids critical for oligomerization of Seipin (Figure 4B), both the luminal and C-terminal regions of ngSeipinL are required for inactivation of SERCA2b.

claim: Myc-tagged ngSeipinL(ΔC) and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL(ΔC) co-expressed existed in closer proximity with each other than Myc-tagged SeipinL(ΔC) and Flag-tagged SeipinL(ΔC) co-expressed.
source: Interestingly, Myc-tagged ngSeipinL(ΔC) and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL(ΔC) co-expressed by transfection at a total of 10.4 ng/cm2 (highest transfection level in this report) existed in closer proximity with each other than Myc-tagged SeipinL(ΔC) and Flag-tagged SeipinL(ΔC) co-expressed by transfection, as shown by PLA (Figure 7A, compare dot plot 4 with dot plot 3).

claim: ngSeipinL(ΔC) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER, did not induce ER stress, and did not induce apoptosis.
source: Nonetheless, ngSeipinL(ΔC) did not decrease [Ca2+] in the ER (Figure 6D, compare bar 13 with bar 2), did not induce ER stress (Figure 7B), and did not induce apoptosis (Figure 7C).
evidence: Experimental observations shown in Figures 6D, 7B, and 7C.

claim: The oligomerization-mediated aggregation propensity and direct interaction with SERCA2b are prerequisites for ngSeipinL to inactivate SERCA2b and thereby induce ER stress and subsequent apoptosis.
source: We concluded that the oligomerization-mediated aggregation propensity and direct interaction with SERCA2b are prerequisites for ngSeipinL to inactivate SERCA2b and thereby induce ER stress and subsequent apoptosis (Figure 7D).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental results and summarized in Figure 7D.

claim: Endogenous Seipin and SERCA2b were colocalized in the ER.
source: Immunofluorescence showed that endogenous Seipin and SERCA2b were colocalized in the ER, which was stained by anti-KDEL antibody, although nuclear region was also stained with anti-SERCA2 antibody, consistent with the presence of SERCA2 in the nuclear envelope (Abrenica and Gilchrist, 2000; Figure 7E).

claim: SERCA2 is present in the nuclear envelope.
source: Immunofluorescence showed that endogenous Seipin and SERCA2b were colocalized in the ER, which was stained by anti-KDEL antibody, although nuclear region was also stained with anti-SERCA2 antibody, consistent with the presence of SERCA2 in the nuclear envelope (Abrenica and Gilchrist, 2000; Figure 7E).

claim: wtSeipinL expressed in Seipin-KO cells showed a typical ER pattern and was colocalized with endogenous SERCA2b.
source: Similarly, wtSeipinL expressed in Seipin-KO cells by transfection at 0.52–10.4 ng/cm2 showed a typical ER pattern and was colocalized with endogenous SERCA2b (Figure 8A(a), panels 1, 3, 5, and 7, transfected cells are surrounded by white broken lines).

claim: ngSeipinL expressed in Seipin-KO cells showed abnormal distribution in enlarged cells.
source: In marked contrast, ngSeipinL expressed in Seipin-KO cells by transfection at 2.60–10.4 ng/cm2 showed abnormal distribution in enlarged cells (Figure 8A(a), panels 4, 6, and 8, transfected cells are surrounded by white broken lines), and accordingly endogenous SERCA2b also showed abnormal distribution.

claim: Endogenous SERCA2b showed abnormal distribution in cells expressing ngSeipinL.
source: In marked contrast, ngSeipinL expressed in Seipin-KO cells by transfection at 2.60–10.4 ng/cm2 showed abnormal distribution in enlarged cells (Figure 8A(a), panels 4, 6, and 8, transfected cells are surrounded by white broken lines), and accordingly endogenous SERCA2b also showed abnormal distribution.

claim: Representative cells expressing ngSeipinL contained strongly double-positive regions, SERCA2b-positive-only regions surrounding the nucleus, and multiple double-negative regions.
source: Representative cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 contained strongly double-positive regions (Figure 8A(b), indicated by white arrows), SERCA2b-positive-only regions surrounding the nucleus (Figure 8A(b), indicated by asterisks), and multiple double-negative regions (Figure 8A(b), surrounded by yellow broken lines).

claim: The percentage of cells with double-negative regions increased in a dose (transfection level of ngSeipinL)-dependent manner.
source: The percentage of cells with double-negative regions increased in a dose (transfection level of ngSeipinL)-dependent manner (Figure 8B(c)).

claim: Strong PLA signals were observed around double-negative regions when Myc-tagged ngSeipinL and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL were co-expressed.
source: It should be noted that strong signals by PLA were observed around double-negative regions when Myc-tagged ngSeipinL and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL were co-expressed by transfection (Figure 4E(a), panel 8-II, double-negative regions are surrounded by yellow broken lines).

claim: Double-negative regions were hardly observed in Seipin-KO cells expressing SeipinL(M6) or ngSeipinL(M6).
source: Importantly, such double-negative regions were hardly observed in Seipin-KO cells expressing SeipinL(M6) or ngSeipinL(M6) by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 (Figure 8A(a, c), compare bar 8 with bars 9 and 10), but were observed in Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL(ΔC) to the same extent as in Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A(a, b), compare bar 3 with bar 2).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Double-negative regions were observed in Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL(ΔC) to the same extent as in Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL.
source: Importantly, such double-negative regions were hardly observed in Seipin-KO cells expressing SeipinL(M6) or ngSeipinL(M6) by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 (Figure 8A(a, c), compare bar 8 with bars 9 and 10), but were observed in Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL(ΔC) to the same extent as in Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A(a, b), compare bar 3 with bar 2).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Induction of double-negative regions correlates well with aggregation propensity of ngSeipinL determined by PLA.
source: Thus, induction of double-negative regions correlates well with aggregation propensity of ngSeipinL determined by PLA (Figure 7D).
evidence: Correlation observed from experimental data summarized in Figure 7D.

claim: Double-negative regions were not stained with anti-GAPDH antibody.
source: Of note, double-negative regions were not stained with anti-GAPDH antibody (Figure 8B).

claim: Seipin-KO cells expressing SeipinL(ΔN), SeipinL(TM1), and SeipinL(TM2) contained double-negative regions similarly to Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL.
source: We found that this distorted morphology of the ER explained the unexpected decrease in [Ca2+] in the ER in Seipin-KO cells expressing SeipinL(ΔN), SeipinL(TM1), and SeipinL(TM2) by transfection (Figure 6D, bars 5, 7, and 10). Such cells contained double-negative regions similarly to Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A(a, b), compare bar 2 with bars 4, 6, and 8), and the percentage of cells with double-negative regions increased in Seipin-KO cells expressing their respective non-glycosylated version (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A(a, b), bars 5, 7, and 9).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Truncation of the N-terminal region or swapping of the transmembrane domain per se adversely affected the structural maintenance of Seipin, making the Seipin mutants aggregation-prone.
source: It is likely that truncation of the N-terminal region or swapping of the transmembrane domain per se adversely affected the structural maintenance of Seipin, making the Seipin mutants aggregation-prone.

claim: Double-negative regions were observed in Seipin-KO cells simultaneously expressing mCherry-SERCA2b and mEGFP-ngSeipinL in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Double-negative regions were also observed in Seipin-KO cells simultaneously expressing mCherry-SERCA2b and mEGFP-ngSeipinL by transfection in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A(a, d), bars 2, 4, and 6) but not in Seipin-KO cells simultaneously expressing mCherry-SERCA2b and mEGFP-wtSeipinL, mEGFP-SeipinL(M6), or mEGFP-ngSeipinL(M6) (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A(a, c, d), bars 5, 7, and 8).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Double-negative regions contained ER-tagBFP.
source: Importantly, such double-negative regions contained ER-tagBFP co-transfected (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A(b)) but not LAMP1-mCherry (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B), and may be identical to organized smooth ER whorl structures observed in cells overexpressing oligomeric fluorescent proteins (Cranfill et al., 2016).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Double-negative regions did not contain LAMP1-mCherry.
source: Importantly, such double-negative regions contained ER-tagBFP co-transfected (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A(b)) but not LAMP1-mCherry (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B), and may be identical to organized smooth ER whorl structures observed in cells overexpressing oligomeric fluorescent proteins (Cranfill et al., 2016).
evidence: Immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Double-negative regions may be identical to organized smooth ER whorl structures observed in cells overexpressing oligomeric fluorescent proteins.
source: Importantly, such double-negative regions contained ER-tagBFP co-transfected (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A(b)) but not LAMP1-mCherry (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B), and may be identical to organized smooth ER whorl structures observed in cells overexpressing oligomeric fluorescent proteins (Cranfill et al., 2016).
evidence: Speculation based on similarity to previously reported structures.

claim: Oligomerization-dependent aggregates of ngSeipinL distorted the shape of the ER, incorporated SERCA2b, and produced double-negative regions in the ER.
source: These results indicate that oligomerization-dependent aggregates of ngSeipinL distorted the shape of the ER, incorporated SERCA2b, and produced double-negative regions in the ER.

claim: Lowered [Ca2+] in the ER of Seipin-KO cells was significantly increased by the introduction of SERCA2b in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Lowered [Ca2+] in the ER of Seipin-KO cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, gray bars) as well as of Seipin-KO cells expressing wtSeipinL by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, blue bars), compared with WT cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, white bar), was significantly increased by the introduction of SERCA2b in a dose-dependent manner, whereas further lowering of [Ca2+] in the ER of Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, red bars) was significantly and slightly increased only by transfection at 20.8 ng/cm2 of SERCA2b, indicating the severe inactivation of SERCA2b by ngSeipinL.
evidence: Experimental observation shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Further lowering of [Ca2+] in the ER of Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL was significantly and slightly increased only by transfection at 20.8 ng/cm2 of SERCA2b, indicating the severe inactivation of SERCA2b by ngSeipinL.
source: Lowered [Ca2+] in the ER of Seipin-KO cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, gray bars) as well as of Seipin-KO cells expressing wtSeipinL by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, blue bars), compared with WT cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, white bar), was significantly increased by the introduction of SERCA2b in a dose-dependent manner, whereas further lowering of [Ca2+] in the ER of Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, red bars) was significantly and slightly increased only by transfection at 20.8 ng/cm2 of SERCA2b, indicating the severe inactivation of SERCA2b by ngSeipinL.

claim: Introduction of SERCA2b had no effect on aggregation propensity between Myc-tagged ngSeipinL and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL determined by PLA.
source: Introduction of SERCA2b (transfection at 20.8 ng/cm2) had no effect on aggregation propensity between Myc-tagged ngSeipinL and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL determined by PLA (Figure 9A) or ngSeipinL-mediated distortion of ER morphology determined by immunofluorescence (Figure 9B).

claim: Introduction of SERCA2b had no effect on ngSeipinL-mediated distortion of ER morphology.
source: Introduction of SERCA2b (transfection at 20.8 ng/cm2) had no effect on aggregation propensity between Myc-tagged ngSeipinL and Flag-tagged ngSeipinL determined by PLA (Figure 9A) or ngSeipinL-mediated distortion of ER morphology determined by immunofluorescence (Figure 9B).

claim: Introduction of SERCA2b significantly mitigated the ER stress induced in Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL.
source: Critically, however, introduction of SERCA2b (transfection at 20.8 ng/cm2) significantly mitigated the ER stress induced in Seipin-KO cells expressing ngSeipinL by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 (Figure 9C).

claim: The growth rate of WT cells slowed by expression of ngSeipinL was rescued by the introduction of SERCA2b.
source: Accordingly, the growth rate of WT cells slowed by expression of ngSeipinL by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 was rescued by the introduction of SERCA2b (transfection at 20.8 ng/cm2) (Figure 9D).

claim: The percentage of apoptotic cells markedly increased by expression of ngSeipin was greatly reduced by introduction of SERCA2b.
source: The percentage of apoptotic cells markedly increased by expression of ngSeipin by transfection at 10.4 ng/cm2 was greatly reduced by introduction of SERCA2b by transfection at 20.8 ng/cm2 (Figure 9E).

claim: ngSeipin induces ER stress and apoptosis through the inactivation of SERCA2b.
source: We concluded that ngSeipin induces ER stress and apoptosis through the inactivation of SERCA2b.

claim: The ratio of expression level of SeipinL to SeipinS in SH-SY5Y cells was estimated to be 4 : 9.
source: The ratio of expression level of SeipinL to SeipinS in SH-SY5Y cells was estimated to be 4 : 9 by quantification of the results of immunoblotting (Figure 10—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Quantification of immunoblotting data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The levels of ngSeipinL and ngSeipinS expressed by transfection in Seipin-KO SH-SY5Y cells would be considered comparable to those of endogenous SeipinL and SeipinS in SH-SY5Y WT cells.
source: Given a transfection efficiency of ~15%, as estimated by transfecting SH-SY5Y cells with plasmid (104 ng/cm2) to express G-CEPIA1er (Figure 10—source data 1), the levels of ngSeipinL and ngSeipinS expressed by transfection in Seipin-KO SH-SY5Y cells would be considered comparable to those of endogenous SeipinL and SeipinS in SH-SY5Y WT cells.
evidence: Inference from transfection efficiency and expression level data.

claim: [Ca2+] in the ER in Seipin-KO SH-SY5Y cells was significantly decreased compared with WT cells.
source: [Ca2+] in the ER in Seipin-KO cells was significantly decreased compared with WT cells (Figure 10A(a, b), compare bar 2 with bar 1).

claim: Expression of wtSeipinL and wtSeipinS in Seipin-KO SH-SY5Y cells rescued the decrease in [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: This decrease was rescued by expression of wtSeipinL and wtSeipinS by transfection (0.62 ng/cm2 and 1.40 ng/cm2, respectively) but further decreased by expression of ngSeipinL and ngSeipinS by transfection (0.62 ng/cm2 and 1.40 ng/cm2, respectively) or by simultaneous expression of wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL (0.31 ng/cm2 each) as well as wtSeipinS and ngSeipinS (0.70 ng/cm2 each) by transfection (Figure 10A(a, b), compare bars 3, 4, and 5 with bars 1 and 2).

claim: Expression of ngSeipinL and ngSeipinS in Seipin-KO SH-SY5Y cells further decreased [Ca2+] in the ER.
source: This decrease was rescued by expression of wtSeipinL and wtSeipinS by transfection (0.62 ng/cm2 and 1.40 ng/cm2, respectively) but further decreased by expression of ngSeipinL and ngSeipinS by transfection (0.62 ng/cm2 and 1.40 ng/cm2, respectively) or by simultaneous expression of wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL (0.31 ng/cm2 each) as well as wtSeipinS and ngSeipinS (0.70 ng/cm2 each) by transfection (Figure 10A(a, b), compare bars 3, 4, and 5 with bars 1 and 2).

claim: Distorted morphology of the ER was observed in Seipin-KO SH-SY5Y cells expressing ngSeipinL and ngSeipinS.
source: Accordingly, distorted morphology of the ER (occurrence of strongly double-positive and double-weak regions) (Figure 10B); induction of ER stress as evidenced by activation of the ERSE (mainly regulated by the ATF6 pathway), UPRE (regulated by the IRE1 and ATF6 pathways), and ATF4 (regulated by the PERK pathway) reporters (Figure 10C); and induction of apoptosis (Figure 10D) were observed in Seipin-KO SH-SY5Y cells expressing ngSeipinL and ngSeipinS (0.62 ng/cm2 and 1.40 ng/cm2, respectively) by transfection (Figure 10B–D, bar 5) and Seipin-KO cells simultaneously expressing wtSeipinL and ngSeipinL (0.31 ng/cm2 each), as well as wtSeipinS and ngSeipinS (0.70 ng/cm2 each) by transfection (Figure 10B–D, bar 4), but not Seipin-KO cells expressing wtSeipinL and wtSeipinS (0.62 ng/cm2 and 1.40 ng/cm2, respectively) by transfection (Figure 10B–D, bar 3).
